newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 3.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 3.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open to large ships on Tuesday even as tropical storm Andres approached the southern Pacific coast, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its meteorological report at 1500 local/2000 GMT.
At the time of the report, Andres was spotted about 72 miles south of Puerto Angel, Oaxaca state. The storm was moving north-northeast and expected to hit land at 1900 local (0000 GMT).
Strong winds along the Pacific Coast shut the largely tourist ports of Huatulco, Puerto Escondido, Acapulco, Puerto Angel, Salina Cruz and Puerto Madero to smaller tourist and fishing craft.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Winds in the north from 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high.

Along the southern coast, Andres was sending strong winds, especially along the coasts of Oaxaca and Chiapas states, where winds 20 to 25 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 28 miles per hour) with waves five to seven feet high.
Tropical storm Andres approaching coast winds of 35 to 40 knots (66 km to 76 km/33 to 44 miles per hour) and waves 12 feet high.

Tropical storm Andres bringing light rains and clouds along coasts of Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche and Yucatan. Winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and waves three to five feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with scattered rains. Winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
